title: SQL injection in product search
description: The q query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE expression. An unauthenticated caller can terminate the string and inject SQL predicates, bypassing the intended search and potentially disclosing data.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201=1-- reaches products.py:40-41, where q is concatenated into the SQL query; the running application returns the product catalogue for this injected search instead of a literal match. Use parameter binding.

title: Stored display name enables SQL injection in admin review report
description: The report query interpolates a database-controlled display_name into SQL. A customer can set display_name through PATCH /account, then a staff request to the report causes that value to be interpreted as SQL, allowing query manipulation and disclosure of unrelated reviews.
evidence: PATCH /account stores attacker-controlled names (auth.py:116-125); admin.py:77-80 builds WHERE r.author_name = '<display_name>' via f-string. A name such as x' OR 1=1 -- changes the query. Use a placeholder.

title: Stored cross-site scripting in review bodies
description: Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review body HTML, and the product template renders persisted bodies with Jinja's safe filter. Script elements and event-handler attributes therefore execute for every visitor viewing the product.
evidence: POST /products/1/reviews with body returned 201 using a valid Bearer token. GET /p/MUG-SPECK returned that exact HTML inside review-body, confirming stored XSS through template line 13. Escape or sanitize review text.

title: Unauthenticated pickle deserialization from basket cookie
description: The basket cookie is client-controlled and is base64-decoded then passed to pickle.loads without authentication. A malicious pickle can execute attacker-chosen Python code whenever /basket, /basket/items, or checkout reads the basket.
evidence: basket.py:15-23 executes pickle.loads on request.cookies[basket]; /basket invokes read_basket without authentication. A malicious pickle encoded as the basket cookie is deserialized on GET /basket before the type check. Use validated JSON or server-side state, never unpickle client input.
